newsitem.title: PERU: Guerrillas give Peru one-hour ultimatum.
newsitem.headline: Guerrillas give Peru one-hour ultimatum.

text.p: Peruvian guerrillas holding 200 hostages at the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima gave the government a one-hour ultimatum at 11:15 A.M. (1615 GMT) on Wednesday to bow to their demands.

"Up to now, there is no harm but within an hour they (the hostages) could suffer harm. We only give him (President Alberto Fujimori) one hour more," a guerrilla spokesman told a local television station from inside the building.
"If within an hour the president does not communicate with us, he will see the results," he said.
Fujimori has so far not commented publicly on the attack.
Countries with ambassadors in the building have urged Fujimori to do all he can to protect the hostages and not to use force to flush out the rebels.

Japan, Germany, Austria, Panama, Venezuela, Bolivia, Brazil, Bulgaria and Cuba confirmed their ambassadors were among the hostages and unconfirmed reports said Spain, South Korea and the European Community had ambassadors inside.
